problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the subspace $S=\text{Span}{{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ where

$$
{a}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 3 \\ 0 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 1 \\ -3 \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{a}_{3}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2 \\ -5 \\ -3\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the distance between $x$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set ${{a}_{1},{a}_{2},{a}_{3}}$ is orthogonal.

examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Distance Between a Vector and a Subspace Spanned by Orthogonal Vectors
examples.problem:
Consider the vector $\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace $S=\textrm{Span}\{ \mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2 \},$ where

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

Find the distance between $\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace $S$ given that the set $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ is orthogonal.
examples.worked_solution:
Since the set $\{\mathbf{a}_1,\mathbf{a}_2\}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $\mathbf{x}$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\textrm{proj}_{S}\,\mathbf{x} 
= \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{a}_1}\mathbf{x} + \textrm{proj}_{\mathbf{a}_2}\mathbf{x}.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $\mathbf{x}$ onto $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_1\}$ and $\textrm{Span}\{\mathbf{a}_2\}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{1}}{{a}_{1}\cdot {a}_{1}}{a}_{1}=\frac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot 2+1\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{1}=\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x & =\frac{x\cdot {a}_{2}}{{a}_{2}\cdot {a}_{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{3\cdot 1+2\cdot (-1)+1\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}{a}_{2}=\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{{a}_{1}}x+{\text{proj}}_{{a}_{2}}x \\  & =\frac{4}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+\frac{2}{3}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{2}{3}(2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]=\overset{^}{x}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, the distance between $\mathbf{x}$ and the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}d(x,\overset{^}{x}) & =‖x-\overset{^}{x}‖ \\  & =\sqrt{({x}_{1}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{1})^{2}+({x}_{2}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{2})^{2}+({x}_{3}-{\overset{^}{x}}_{3})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{(3-2)}^{2}+{(2-2)}^{2}+{(1-2)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
Consider the vector $x$ and the plane $r=sv+tw,$ where $s,t\in R,$ and

$$
v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],\,w=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}],\,\,x=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 3 \\ 0\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the plane given that $v⊥w.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our plane passes through the origin, it defines the subspace $S=\text{Span}{v,w}$ in ${R}^{3}.$ 
And, since the set ${v,w}$ is orthogonal, the orthogonal projection of $x$ onto the subspace $S$ is given by

$$
{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x.
$$

So, we first find the orthogonal projections of $x$ onto $\text{Span}{{a}_{1}}$ and $\text{Span}{{a}_{2}}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{v}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot v}{v\cdot v}v=\frac{3\cdot 1+3\cdot 1+0\cdot 1}{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}}v=2[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}] \\ {\text{proj}}_{w}\,x & =\frac{x\cdot w}{w\cdot w}w=\frac{3\cdot 2+3\cdot (-1)+0\cdot (-1)}{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}}w=\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have that

$$
\begin{aligned}{\text{proj}}_{S}\,x & ={\text{proj}}_{v}\,x+{\text{proj}}_{w}\,x \\  & =[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+\frac{1}{2}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =\frac{1}{2}(2[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]) \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ \frac{3}{2} \\ \frac{3}{2}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
